Scale Overload: SEC Proposed Major Expansion of Scaled Disclosure Requirements

status_summary: No three-category regime was found. The SEC proposed on 2026-05-21 to consolidate reporting companies into two filer categories and extend scaled disclosure to all non-accelerated filers, with later deadlines for the smallest; the proposal, also tracked in c27-04, is a parallel step because it creates no separate intermediate category or secondary-market tiers. H.R. 3343, the Greenlighting Growth Act, which trims financial statement requirements for emerging growth companies, passed the House on 2025-07-21 and was referred to a Senate committee on 2025-07-22.

timeline.event: H.R. 3343, the Greenlighting Growth Act, is introduced; it limits the financial statements an emerging growth company must provide.
The House passes H.R. 3343 as amended by voice vote under suspension of the rules; it is referred to the Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee on 2025-07-22.

The SEC proposal to enhance emerging growth company accommodations and simplify filer status is published at 91 FR 30086 (FR Doc. 2026-10222, RIN 3235-AN40, File No. S7-2026-18); it would group reporting companies into two filer categories (large accelerated and non-accelerated filers), extend scaled disclosure to all non-accelerated filers and give the smallest non-accelerated filers (total assets of 35 million dollars or less) longer report deadlines, with comments due 2026-07-20.

title: Reform securities disclosure into private, intermediate and public firm categories
uncertainties: Searches performed by the researchers: web searches for 119th Congress bills creating a new issuer category, which surfaced H.R. 3343 and no three-category bill, and for an adopted final filer status rule, which returned only proposal summaries. Other bills in the House capital formation package, and Regulation A, crowdfunding and private-market proposals, were not individually searched. The Federal Register page for the proposal (91 FR 30086, FR Doc. 2026-10222) was read in review except roughly its last 15,000 characters; the Federal Register API record for the document lists it as a proposed rule with no effective date and no linked final rule as of 2026-10-17. The proposal's smallest non-accelerated filer group is a deadline sub-tier within one category, not a separate disclosure category. c27-04 tracks the other May 2026 proposals. A law-firm summary states that the proposal has no separate third filer category.
